questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Forces?
questions.answer: Force is a vector that changes the momentum of a particle. The net force is the vector sum of all forces acting on the particle. Newton's second law states that net force equals the rate of change of momentum. When mass is constant, this becomes the familiar relation between force and acceleration.

questions.prompt: What does \(m\) mean in Forces?
questions.answer: In Forces, \(m\) means mass of the particle. Its unit is kg.

questions.prompt: Forces \(4\mathbf i\) N, \(-\mathbf i+2\mathbf j\) N, and \(-3\mathbf j\) N act on a particle. Find the net force.
questions.answer: Add components: \(\mathbf F_{\text{net}}=(4-1)\mathbf i+(2-3)\mathbf j=3\mathbf i-\mathbf j\) N. This vector sum is the force used in Newton's second law.

questions.prompt: A \(2\) kg particle has acceleration \(3\mathbf i-4\mathbf j\) \(m s^{-2}\). Find the net force.
questions.answer: Use \(\mathbf F_{\text{net}}=m\mathbf a\). The force is \(2(3\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)=6\mathbf i-8\mathbf j\) N.
